title: Pipeline failure isolation: IPFS write failure prevents partial state
description: transit/src/peering/pipeline.rs:182-185: the IPFS write is step 1 and aborts the entire pipeline on failure. msgid_map insert, log appends, and gossip publish never execute if IPFS write fails. This is the correct failure model — partial state (article in log but not in IPFS, or in IPFS but not in log) is worse than a clean abort. The docstring captures this: 'Returns Err immediately if the IPFS write fails — nothing is committed.' A future contributor might suggest reordering (do the cheap DB operations first, IPFS last) to reduce latency. That would be wrong: the CID is unknown until after the IPFS write, and all downstream operations depend on it. The current order is correct and should be defended.
